images.title: Squares tile, circles leave gaps
images.purpose: Show on two equal trays that 12 square tiles cover a tray with no gaps and 6 round tiles leave gaps between them.
images.composition: Two equal trays side by side, squares on the left, circles on the right, each with a plain caption.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. At the top, centred at x 728 and y 62, the heading Tiles on a tray in dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif (44 px). LEFT tray: a rectangle 400 by 300 px at x 130 to 530 and y 230 to 530 with a thin grey #6B7280 outline (4 px) and a white inside. Inside it exactly 12 square tiles in 3 rows of 4, every tile 100 by 100 px, filled teal #0072B2 with a thin dark #2B2B2B outline (3 px), edge to edge so there is no gap and no overlap; the top left corners of the tiles are at x [130, 230, 330, 430] and y [230, 330, 430]. RIGHT tray: the same rectangle, 400 by 300 px, at x 830 to 1230 and y 230 to 530, with the same grey outline and a white inside. Inside it exactly 6 round tiles in 2 rows of 3, every tile a circle of 100 px diameter filled amber #E69F00 with a thin dark #2B2B2B outline (3 px), with the centres at x [897, 1030, 1163] and y [305, 455], so there are visible white gaps between the circles and at the corners of the tray. Under the left tray, centred at x 330 and y 590, the caption Squares; under the right tray, centred at x 1030 and y 590, the caption Circles, both in dark #1F2937 bold (40 px). In all 2 trays, 12 squares and 6 circles. No number and no other text anywhere. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
a tray with a number of squares other than 12 or of circles other than 6, or circles that touch with no gap
any number or answer written anywhere in the frame
images.takeaway: Squares fit edge to edge with no gaps and no overlaps, so they tile; circles leave gaps, so they do not.
images.description: Two equal trays: 12 square tiles in 3 rows of 4 cover one with no gaps, and 6 round tiles in 2 rows of 3 leave gaps on the other.
images.context: Concept image for Tiles That Cover Without Gaps. It follows the idea of the tables in your maths book (squares cover a top, circles leave gaps) and uses the numbers of this concept's own example: 12 squares and 6 circles.
images.teaching_notes: Let the student point at the gaps between the circles and say why the squares leave none. The slip to watch: thinking that circles pushed close together would tile.

image_decisions.why: The two trays put the difference between a shape that tiles and one that does not in one look.
